description: The behaviour contract: what each interactive element must do in each state, and how the change moves. Nowind styles state through markup (aria-pressed, aria-selected, aria-current, aria-expanded, open, aria-invalid, disabled) and the variants that read it, plus the state layer (state) for hover and press. The examples lint checks the static rules; node scripts/review.mjs behaviour forces each state on every interactive element in headless Chromium (CSS.forcePseudoState over the DevTools protocol) and compares computed styles.
elements: a[href], button, summary, select, input (not hidden), textarea, label holding a checkbox or radio, and [role=button|tab|option|menuitem|switch|checkbox|radio]

states.rule: Shows a visible change: a fill, a state layer, a text or border colour, an underline. A link in running text may rely on its underline.
Differs from hover where the element shows a press: the state layer deepens (0.12 to 0.16), or the fill steps.
Draws a ring outside the box: the reset's 2px accent outline at a 2px offset, or a ring of the element's own. Never removed without a replacement.

states.trigger: aria-pressed, aria-selected, aria-checked, aria-current, aria-expanded, open, :checked
states.rule: Differs from hover, so a chosen item never reads as a hovered one. Each on-state variant has the attribute that fires it.
Does not react to hover or press, shows cursor not-allowed, and fades (opacity) or quiets its text.
Shows on the field or its box: a danger border.
Quieter than a typed value (fg step 8 or 9 against 12).

motion.rule: A change in colour, opacity, shadow or transform between states transitions: interactive elements get it from the reset, anything else names a transition class.
Durations and easings come from the motion tokens (--motion-duration, --motion-easing and the duration-* and ease-* classes); no other durations.
Never transition all, and never a layout property (width, height, margin, padding, inset).
Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce every transition and animation is cut to a moment (the reset).

rules.rule: An element with an on-state variant (pressed:, selected:, current:, expanded:, open:, invalid:, disabled:) carries the attribute or element that fires it.
Every enabled interactive element shows a visible change on hover.
Where an element has a state layer or a pressed fill, press differs from hover.
Every interactive element draws a visible ring on focus-visible.
An element in an on state looks different from the same element hovered at rest.
A disabled element does not change on hover.
An interactive element is at least 24 by 24px, or sits clear of other targets by that much (WCAG 2.5.8). Links in running text are exempt.
Each transition's duration is a motion token's, its easing a token's, and it names no layout property and not all.
